Apple will, as usual, unveil the iPhone 18 series this September, but the launch arrangements will in several ways resemble the atypical pattern seen during the pandemic in 2020.

Aspects in which this autumn's iPhone unveiling will differ from Apple's usual approach

Apple has many highly successful products, but the iPhone remains its flagship and accounts for a large share of overall revenue.

It is therefore understandable that Apple is committed to maintaining a steady iPhone release cadence. Keeping a predictable new-product schedule reassures both Wall Street and consumers.

Generally speaking, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September, typically introducing four models, all of which go on sale later that same month.

The COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 thoroughly disrupted this routine.

That autumn's iPhones were not announced until October, and only two models went on sale initially, with the other two following in November.

This year, rumours suggest Apple is planning a similarly unconventional launch arrangement.

Although the expectation of a September event remains unchanged, not all new iPhones will go on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models may be released first — the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to be unveiled in September, but reports suggest its launch could be slightly delayed, possibly arriving several weeks after the Pro models.

In terms of the total number of iPhone models, Apple may also break from its usual practice.

If rumours that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be pushed back to spring 2027 prove accurate, only three new models will debut this autumn — the smallest autumn iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether driven by strategic considerations, a global memory chip shortage, or production challenges for the new foldable design, Apple's autumn 2026 event could echo 2020 on several fronts.
